correctness.rationale: Subtract the lower-right scalar entry to identify M₂(R)/RI with triples in R³. Two matrices commute iff the three alternating minors of their triples vanish. A nonscalar reduction supplies a unit in the triple, forcing every commuting triple to be its unique multiple, with an unrestricted scalar partner; there are q^(2d+2) such partners. For scalar reduction the triple lies in m³. Its d residue coefficient triples span a subspace of k³. The residue of a commuting triple is unrestricted when the span has rank 0, belongs to a fixed line at rank 1, and must vanish at rank at least 2. The respective tuple counts are q^d, (q²+q+1)(q^(2d)−q^d), and the complement, including the scalar coordinates of all coefficient matrices. All residue partners lift freely in this case. This gives all four distinct, occupied sizes for d≥2, without a coefficient-field assumption. Scalar–scalar residue pairs give q² q^(8d) pairs. Each other commuting residue pair has a nonscalar member; its partner is a linear combination of it and I. Choose commuting lifts and linearize: the commutator in the radical coordinates has rank 2d, so each gives q^(6d) lifts. There are q⁶+q⁵−q³−q² such residue pairs. Division by q^(8d+8) and comparison with the scalar–scalar contribution give the claimed probability and conditional rate. The frozen C++ checker and recorded output were inspected rather than executed. Its mixed-characteristic example is d=1. A separate direct-product enumeration at /workspace/branches/340f9e15-cb89-4981-91d3-5419a61b0ce0/independent_squarezero_ring_check.py (arguments 8 2) checked all 16,777,216 ordered pairs in the actual mixed-characteristic d=2 case Z/4[e]/(2e,e²), finding 606,208 commuting pairs and size multiplicities 64:3584, 512:336, 1024:168, 4096:8. That check corroborates, but is not the all-q,d proof.

originality.rationale: Distinct indexed record b47fa25cabce is stated for GL₂(R), but its Proof §§1–3 already establishes the full-matrix facts that mechanically imply this census. In its scalar-reduction rows the exact coefficient-tuple counts and the full simultaneous commutant algebras are identified before units are counted: M₂(k), a two-dimensional quadratic algebra, or kI. Replace q−1 choices of nonzero residue scalar by q, merge the three quadratic types, and replace the unit counts by q⁴, q², q, respectively; every commuting residue partner still has all q^(4d) lifts, by the same square-zero equation in §2. For every nonscalar residue (including singular ones) the cyclic argument in §1 gives the full two-dimensional commutant, and the lift αI+βA works without invertibility; retaining all residues gives exactly (q⁴−q)q^(4d) elements for the first row. The totals and concentration are direct arithmetic on the resulting census, since the scalar–scalar residue contribution is q² q^(8d). This is coverage by the indexed proof, not an assertion that the GL₂ statement alone gives ring centralizer orders, nor a priority inference from the same-day dates.
residual_risks: Same-day timestamps do not determine priority; the decision is about documented mathematical coverage.

value.rationale: The all-matrix vs. unit-group distinction is meaningful, and the full-ring conditional probability is well defined. But computing the ring census here changes only which already classified algebra elements are counted, and its asymptotic interpretation follows by summing rows and separating the automatic scalar–scalar lifts. The frozen result does not supply a substantive exact-invariant advance beyond that implication. The extra small mixed-characteristic computation corroborates the proof, but does not change that assessment.
